clue.text: Divert funds quietly during backing of man's cricket side

indicators.note: during places the quiet letter in the middle of the turned-round possessive
backing of tells us the possessive word is read from right to left

parts.note: a man's thing is his
P (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
the on side is one half of a cricket field, also called leg side

explanation.surface: Someone embezzles money on the quiet while sponsoring a men's cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing of' gives SIH, and 'during' sets P in it. The surface 'backing' suggests sponsorship of a team, but here it means reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To siphon off money is to draw it away secretly for another use.

clue.text: Composer is opposing single covered by blues fake

indicators.note: opposing suggests facing the other way, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: covered by puts the lone letter inside the shuffled word
fake means counterfeit or made up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a single record wrapped in a counterfeit blues track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposing' gives SI and 'fake' gives BELUS; 'covered by' sets I in that to make BELIUS. 'single' and 'blues' suggest records, not a numeral and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Sibelius was the Finnish composer of Finlandia and seven symphonies.

clue.text: Disguise weight with big hairstyle in boat

indicators.note: in places the weight and hairstyle inside the boat

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed river boat
a ton is a unit of weight
an Afro is a large rounded hairstyle

explanation.surface: Someone with a heavy load and a huge hairdo sits in a boat trying to go unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: A PUNT is the flat boat poled along rivers such as the Cam at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a front is to assume a false appearance, a way of disguising true feelings.

clue.text: Cooker demonstrated has price dropped

indicators.note: dropped means the price abbreviation is let go from the longer word

parts.note: something demonstrated has been proven

explanation.surface: A kitchen appliance has been shown to work and its price has been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is the enclosed part of a cooker used for baking and roasting.

clue.text: TV doctor once broke rake by burial-place

indicators.note: by means next to, so the burial place stands beside the shuffled garden tool

parts.note: a tomb is a place of burial

indicators.note: broke signals that the letters of the tool are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A former TV medic snapped a garden rake beside a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' rearranges RAKE as AKER. Tom Baker played the Doctor in the BBC's Doctor Who from 1974 to 1981.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Baker was the fourth actor to play the Doctor, the hero of a long-running BBC series.

clue.text: Criminal who's last joining F wing in US

indicators.note: who's last means the final letter belonging to the word who

parts.note: taken as written
in American English a car's wing is called a fender

explanation.surface: A crook is the last to join the F wing of an American prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's last' picks O, the final letter of 'who'. The surface wing is a prison block; the wordplay wing is the panel over a car's wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is someone who commits a crime, a synonym for criminal.

clue.text: Fanzine perhaps withdrawn a day after second game

indicators.note: after places the reversed magazine following the support word

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it

indicators.note: withdrawn suggests pulling back, so the magazine word is read backwards

parts.note: a fanzine is an example of a mag, a magazine
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday, a day

explanation.surface: A fan magazine is pulled from sale a day after the second match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' turns MAG into GAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game for two played with dice and counters.

clue.text: 1960s movie makes millions, before losing

indicators.note: losing means the abbreviation letters are dropped from the word makes

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million or millions
A, short for Latin ante, stands for before

explanation.surface: A sixties film earns a fortune before going on to lose money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' strips M and A from MAKES. Kes is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a Yorkshire boy and his kestrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Kes is the 1969 Ken Loach film adapted from Barry Hines's novel about a kestrel.

clue.text: Merchant with no time to digest European academic

indicators.note: to digest means to take something inside, so one letter goes into the trimmed merchant
with no means the time abbreviation is removed from the merchant

parts.note: a merchant is a trader

explanation.surface: A merchant too busy to take in a European academic's ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' takes T from TRADER to leave RADER; 'to digest' puts E inside it. In British universities a reader ranks just below a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities a reader is a senior lecturer, the rank just below professor.

clue.text: Jack reversed truck into Kate, who's gutted

indicators.note: into shows the turned vehicle going inside the emptied name
gutted means the inside is removed, leaving only the outside letters of Kate
reversed tells us the vehicle word is read backwards

parts.note: a van is a small truck

explanation.surface: Jack backed his truck into Kate, who was devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns VAN into NAV, and 'gutted' leaves K and E of Kate.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is the jack in a pack of playing cards, and also a rogue.

clue.text: Wading bird, part gull

parts.note: a bit is a part of something
a tern is a seabird related to the gull

explanation.surface: A long-legged bird that is partly a seagull.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like marsh bird known for its booming call.

clue.text: Such breaks disrupt most of Italian car plant

indicators.note: disrupt means to break into, so the shuffled word sits inside the shortened car
most of means the last letter of the car name is dropped

parts.note: Fiat is an Italian car maker

indicators.note: breaks signals the letters of the word are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Breakdowns like these interrupt most of production at an Italian car factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' gives UCHS; 'most of' leaves FIA, and 'disrupt' sets UCHS inside. 'plant' looks like a factory but is a garden shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a shrub grown for its drooping purple and red flowers.

clue.text: English river, primarily like French one

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letter of like is taken

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for one

explanation.surface: An English river that is mostly like a French one.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lune flows through Cumbria and Lancashire, reaching the sea at Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lune is a river in north-west England flowing through Lancaster.

clue.text: Accomplished area for flowers without borders — daringly innovative

indicators.note: without borders means the outermost letters at each edge of the combined words are cut

parts.note: a savant is a learned, accomplished person
a garden is an area where flowers are grown

explanation.surface: A skilled gardener plants a borderless flower bed, a bold new idea.
explanation.walkthrough: SAVANT and GARDEN joined lose their outermost letters, S and N. 'borders' plays on flower borders.
explanation.definitionFit: The avant-garde are the pioneers of new and experimental ideas, especially in the arts.

clue.text: Film director delivered line Glaswegian possibly said

parts.note: to be delivered from something is to be rid of it
a ley line is an imagined straight line linking ancient sites

indicators.note: said means the word is heard rather than read, so its sound is used

parts.note: a person from Glasgow is an example of a Scot

explanation.surface: A film director delivers a line that a Glaswegian might have spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: Ridley Scott directed Alien, Blade Runner and Gladiator.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridley Scott is the English director of films such as Alien and Gladiator.

clue.text: Police branch meddlesome about US writer

parts.note: the Bill is British slang for the police
BR is the abbreviation for branch

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the meddlesome word is read backwards

parts.note: a meddlesome person is nosy

explanation.surface: A police unit pokes into the affairs of an American author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NOSY into YSON. THE BILL is British slang for the police, also a long-running TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Bryson is the American-born author of travel books such as Notes from a Small Island.

clue.text: Dirty fellow leaves amusement showground

indicators.note: leaves means the fellow abbreviation departs from the showground

parts.note: a funfair is a showground of rides and amusements

explanation.surface: A grubby man walks out of the fairground.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty play is unfair play, against the rules or sporting spirit.

clue.text: Producer of rum shorts originated here

definitions.meaning: the island makes and sells its own rum, such as Gosling's
knee-length tailored shorts are named after this Atlantic island

explanation.definitionFit: Bermuda is an Atlantic island known for rum and for knee-length Bermuda shorts.

clue.text: Learner driver seen in City repeatedly jerking, ranging wide

indicators.note: seen in means the learner letter appears inside the doubled city code
repeatedly means the city abbreviation is used twice

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
L is the plate shown by a learner driver
a tic is an involuntary jerking movement

explanation.surface: A learner driver keeps lurching through the City streets.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L plate; EC is the City of London's postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclectic tastes are wide-ranging, drawn from many diverse sources.

clue.text: Brood somewhere Caribbean in middle of winter

indicators.note: in places the Caribbean island inside the trimmed season
middle of means the season loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island, an example of somewhere there

explanation.surface: Someone sulks about being in the Caribbean in the depths of winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' cuts WINTER to INTE. 'Brood' looks like a noun or a sulk, but is the verb of sitting on eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds brood or incubate eggs by sitting on them to keep them warm.

clue.text: Artist cut back hair

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: An artist has his hair trimmed short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LOP into POL. Jackson Pollock was the American drip painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackson Pollock was an American abstract expressionist painter.

clue.text: After work's over, adolescent finds booze illicitly

indicators.note: after places the teenager following the turned work
over means turned over, so the work abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
a teen is an adolescent

explanation.surface: Once work is done, a teenager gets hold of alcohol on the sly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns OP into PO. Poteen is Irish whiskey distilled illicitly.
explanation.definitionFit: Poteen is Irish spirit traditionally distilled illegally from potatoes or grain.

clue.text: Revise two plays hampered by drink

indicators.note: hampered by means surrounded and held back, so the drink wraps the rearranged number

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: plays means the letters move about freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student cramming for two plays is held back by drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' gives WOT, held inside by 'hampered by'. SWOT UP is British slang for studying hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To swot up is British slang for studying hard, revising for an exam.

clue.text: Love to enter competition, with prize ultimately a car

indicators.note: to enter means the zero letter goes into the competition

parts.note: a cup is a sporting competition
love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so the last letter of prize is taken

explanation.surface: Someone would love to enter a contest with a car as the eventual prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupé is a two-door car with a fixed roof.

clue.text: Getting through pasty, European Merlot's drunk — it's fruity

indicators.note: getting through means going inside, so the rearranged letters sit within the pale word

parts.note: pasty means pale-faced, or wan

indicators.note: drunk signals the letters are tipsy and jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A pale-faced European works through a bottle of Merlot, a fruity wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles E and MERLOT into TERMELO, which 'Getting through' sets between the A and N of the pale word. 'it's fruity' reads as wine-tasting talk, but defines the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A watermelon is a large juicy fruit, so it is fruity by its nature.

clue.text: Thesaurus contains scriptural character

indicators.note: contains signals the name lies within the letters of the reference book

explanation.surface: A thesaurus lists a figure from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau is the elder twin of Jacob in Genesis, who sold his birthright.

clue.text: Group of women — male's elusive target at dog track

indicators.note: elusive means escaping, so the male abbreviation slips away from the group

parts.note: a harem is a group of women in a household
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Women's group, with the man evasive, chasing the target at the greyhound stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: At greyhound tracks the dogs chase a mechanical hare.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyhounds race after a mechanical lure called a hare.

clue.text: Department finally shifted rats in passage

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of department
shifted signals the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A department eventually relocated the rats into a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' rearranges RATS and IN as RANSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means passage from one place to another.

clue.text: Trouble — that's beer talking

indicators.note: talking means the word is heard, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Problems arise when the drink starts doing the talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to trouble or afflict, as in what's ailing you.

clue.text: Reportedly ferry the French musical instrument

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the ferry company name is heard

parts.note: P&O is a British ferry company, said as pee-and-oh
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: Apparently a ferry carries the French musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O is a well-known British ferry operator; spoken quickly it sounds like PIANO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianola is a player piano, worked mechanically by perforated paper rolls.

clue.text: Clothing Marco starts to notice, knocking around City

parts.note: Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller

indicators.note: around means the two opening letters wrap the city code
starts to means the first letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Marco Polo begins to notice himself knocking about a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives N and K, which go 'around' EC to make NECK. A polo neck is a high turned-over collar, called a turtleneck in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A polo neck is a sweater with a high close-fitting turned-over collar.

clue.text: Dog — it's retrieved within minute

indicators.note: within means the reversed word sits inside the small word

parts.note: minute means tiny, or wee

indicators.note: retrieved suggests bringing back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A dog fetches something back in a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrieved' turns ITS into STI. A Westie is a West Highland white terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Westie is a West Highland white terrier, a small Scottish breed.
